summary: The oracle sink connector compiles and passes all unit tests. However, 2 significant runtime bugs were found: (1) Value::Unchanged maps to NULL in MERGE, causing data loss on UPDATE with TOAST columns, (2) DataType::Time wrapped in TO_TIMESTAMP without date component causes Oracle ORA-01861. Also 2 minor issues (empty string edge case and dead code).

findings.root_cause: write_batch() uses the same MERGE path for both Insert and Update records. For Update records, `Value::Unchanged` columns (PG TOAST optimization — columns not changed in the UPDATE) are mapped to `"NULL"` by `value_to_oracle_expr` (types.rs:232). The `generate_merge()` function (merge_generator.rs:72-91) always sets ALL non-PK columns in the UPDATE SET clause. Result: the MERGE unconditionally overwrites unchanged TOAST columns with NULL, causing data loss.
findings.fix: Two-part fix: (1) In write_batch, for Update records, filter out columns whose values are `Value::Unchanged` before calling `build_using_select`. (2) Modify `generate_merge` to accept an optional filtered column list for the UPDATE SET clause, excluding Unchanged columns. Alternative minimal fix: change `value_to_oracle_expr(Value::Unchanged)` to return `"DEFAULT"` and modify the MERGE to use `COALESCE(src.col, dst.col)` pattern — but Oracle MERGE does not allow COALESCE across USING/DST boundaries, so filtering is required.

findings.root_cause: is_date_column() returns true for DataType::Time (line 13). This causes time-only values like '14:30:00' to go through value_to_oracle_date_expr(), which wraps them in TO_TIMESTAMP('14:30:00', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'). Oracle rejects this with ORA-01861 because '14:30:00' has no YYYY-MM-DD component matching the format mask. Also, data_type_to_oracle maps Time to 'INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND(0)' which is semantically a duration, not wall-clock time.
findings.fix: Option A: Remove DataType::Time from is_date_column() and implement proper INTERVAL DAY TO SECOND literal generation (INTERVAL '0 14:30:00' DAY TO SECOND). Option B: Map DataType::Time to VARCHAR2(8) in data_type_to_oracle and handle as string. Option A has better type fidelity but is more work. If Option A is chosen, update both is_date_column() and value_to_oracle_date_expr() to handle Time separately from Timestamp.

findings.root_cause: BUG-6 from BUGS.md: The string cleaning logic in value_to_oracle_date_expr() can produce an empty string for unusual timezone-only inputs (e.g., Value::String('+00')). The trim_end_matches() closure removes '+', '-', ':', and digits from the end of the string, which can strip everything. This produces TO_TIMESTAMP('', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') which fails in Oracle.
findings.fix: Add guard: if cleaned.is_empty() { return 'NULL'.to_string(); } after the string cleaning block (after line 55).

findings.root_cause: connect_sync() and find_schema() are defined but never called. connect_sync (line 125) is dead because connection is done inline in write_batch and validate_connection. find_schema (line 133) is dead because schema lookup is done inline in write_batch via source_schemas.iter().find(). group_by_table (line 138) is used only in tests but never in production — write_batch does its own grouping inline (lines 342-352). The whole schema_tracking.rs module is imported but its types (SchemaState, initialize_state) are never used — the SOURCE_SCHEMAS static OnceLock is used instead.
findings.fix: Remove connect_sync(), find_schema() dead code. Remove or deprecate group_by_table() (or use it in write_batch instead of the inline grouping). Remove schema_tracking.rs module or integrate it with the OnceLock pattern. These do NOT cause runtime failures but create confusion and maintenance burden.
findings.test_to_verify: cargo check --features oracle-sink,default -p dbmazz 2>&1 | grep -c warning

findings.root_cause: Unused import `info` from tracing crate. This warning exists regardless of the oracle-sink feature flag — it's a pre-existing issue in the shared WAL handler code.
findings.fix: Remove `info` from the use statement: change `use tracing::{error, info};` to `use tracing::error;`.

findings.root_cause: PG_EPOCH_OFFSET_USEC is hardcoded for PostgreSQL's epoch (2000-01-01). When MySQL is the source, commit timestamps use Unix epoch (1970-01-01), so adding PG_EPOCH_OFFSET_USEC produces commit timestamps ~30 years in the future. This affects replication lag calculation for MySQL→Oracle pipelines. Pre-existing bug not introduced by the Oracle sink.
findings.fix: The pipeline should receive the source type and conditionally apply PG_EPOCH_OFFSET_USEC only when the source is PostgreSQL.

findings.root_cause: PG OID 114 (json, not jsonb) is mapped to DataType::Jsonb. PG's json preserves key ordering and duplicate keys; jsonb does not. This is a semantic type slippage that affects Oracle DDL generation. Pre-existing issue not introduced by the Oracle sink.
findings.fix: Map OID 114 → DataType::Json and OID 3802 → DataType::Jsonb separately.

findings.root_cause: OID 790 (Money) is handled in convert_pg_value (returns Value::Decimal) but NOT included in pg_type_to_data_type, so it falls through to the default DataType::String. For the Oracle sink, column_type(DataType::String, Some(790)) calls pg_oid_to_oracle_type(790) which returns 'CLOB' (not in any match arm → catches _ => 'CLOB'). The column is CLOB but values are Decimal — works functionally (Oracle accepts numbers in CLOB) but semantically wrong. Pre-existing converter gap.
findings.fix: Add 790 → DataType::Decimal { precision: ... } to pg_type_to_data_type() in converter.rs, or add 790 to pg_oid_to_oracle_type() in types.rs to map to NUMBER.
findings.test_to_verify: Not oracle-sink specific — pre-existing gap in converter
